currentFocus.title: Consolidate Browser SQL requirements and end-to-end acceptance scenarios

stageSummary.planned: browser constraints → official capability research → target architecture → detailed planning → implementation decomposition → GitHub execution structure → final plan audit

baselineSource.result: V1 remains the frozen verified reference for browser collection, integrity, atomic persistence behavior, viewer recovery and browser runtime patterns.

planningBootstrap.result: Current responsibilities, reusable contracts, replaceable implementation choices, stale SQL planning and major unknowns were inventoried before target architecture design.

architectureConstraint.rule: Browser SQL is fixed for this planning cycle. localhost/Node/.NET/native database paths are not active candidates or backlog items.

engineSelection.requiredNextEvidence: Official capability research follows requirements consolidation and browser-constraint planning.

verification.specImpact: No runtime behavior changed. Product/planning/decision documentation now treats Browser-only SQL as the current architecture constraint. Browser SQL normative implementation specs do not exist yet and are intentionally deferred until target design is complete.

next.action: Planning Phase B: consolidate Browser SQL requirements and define end-to-end acceptance scenarios.
steps: Extract stable requirements from product docs and the Browser SQL planning brief without creating duplicate authorities.
Classify material items as fixed decision, design requirement, acceptance behavior, assumption or unknown.

Define end-to-end acceptance scenarios for committed-cycle visibility, arbitrary SQL replacement, configurable query cadence, 0..N results, query failure isolation, refresh/reopen and raw/NULL preservation.
Define explicit planning non-goals so trading formula, entry/exit and implementation details stay out of scope.
Do not start implementation or external capability research beyond what is required to resolve requirement ambiguity.

history.rule: Superseded architecture/research plans remain cold history and do not carry current progress.
